setup.game.workshop.items.other: {n} items on disk, {total} listed by Steam
setup.warning.steam.manifest-leftover: Steam left temporary copies of the game manifest next to the real one. They were ignored; they are harmless.
setup.warning.steam.userdir-version-mism: Your user data was last written by another game version than the installed one. Start the game once to refresh it.
setup.warning.steam.library-offline: A Steam library folder is not reachable, for example an unplugged drive.

setup.warning.steam.workshop-different-l: The workshop folder is in a different Steam library than the game.
setup.override.title: Overrides
setup.override.hint: Detection picks these by itself. Choose a folder only when it picked the wrong one. Clearing an override returns to detection.
setup.sources.title: Mod folders
setup.sources.hint: Folders RimStudio reads mods from, in scan order. Add as many of your own as you like. RimStudio only reads them.
setup.sources.empty.title: No mod folders yet
setup.sources.empty.hint: Run detection first, or add a folder of your own.
setup.source.drive: On drive {name}. If the drive is unplugged the folder shows as not reachable.
setup.add.title: Add a mod folder
setup.add.error: The folder could not be checked
setup.add.label: Label
setup.add.label.hint: Optional. The folder name is used when empty.
setup.probe.warn.no-mods-found: No mods were found in this folder.
setup.probe.warn.mods-found-deeper: Mods were found deeper than the suggested depth.
setup.probe.warn.ambiguous-layout: The layout is ambiguous: this could be one mod or a folder of mods.
setup.probe.warn.path-is-link: This path is a link to another folder.
setup.probe.warn.unreachable: Part of this folder could not be read.
setup.probe.overlap: This folder overlaps a folder already in the list, so the same mods would appear twice.
setup.probe.offline: The folder was not found or cannot be reached.
setup.remove.title: Remove this folder from the list
setup.remove.nofiles: No files are touched. The folder and its mods stay exactly where they are.
setup.scan.title: Library scan
setup.scan.hint: Reads the About files, load folders and definitions of every enabled folder. A scan reuses what has not changed; a full rescan reads everything again.
setup.scan.none: No scan has run in this session.
setup.scan.cancelled: The scan was cancelled; the result is partial.
setup.scan.custom-only.title.one: {n} mod exists only in your own folder
setup.scan.custom-only.title.other: {n} mods exist only in your own folders
setup.scan.custom-only.body: The game cannot load a mod that sits only in one of your own folders. Link it into the game Mods folder or copy it there before you enable it.
setup.dup.title: Duplicate package ids
setup.dup.none: No package id is used by more than one mod.
setup.dup.summary: {groups} package ids are used by more than one mod; {skipped} copies are skipped.
setup.dup.game.not-visible: The game does not see it
setup.dup.reason.available: It is the only copy the game can see
setup.dup.reason.source-priority: The source with the higher priority wins
setup.dup.reason.path-order: It comes first by folder path
setup.scan.diag.title: Diagnostics
setup.scan.diag.none: No problems found in the scanned mods.
setup.scan.diag.truncated: More problems exist than are listed.
setup.diag.about.no-supported-versions: The mod's About file lists no supported versions, so the game cannot tell which versions it is for.
setup.diag.about.field-dropped: An About field was ignored because it could not be read.
setup.diag.loadfolders.ignored-attribute: A LoadFolders entry uses an attribute the game does not read, so the condition has no effect.
setup.diag.scan.no-about: A folder looked like a mod but has no About file.
setup.diag.scan.dir-unreadable: A folder could not be read.
setup.diag.scan.def-file-broken: A definition file is not valid XML and was skipped.
setup.diag.scan.package-id-missing: A mod has no package id.
setup.ce.title: Combat Extended
setup.ce.hint: The Combat Extended patch generator needs Combat Extended in your library. The designer itself never needs it.
setup.ce.name: Name
setup.ce.not-loadable: The game cannot load this copy as it is
setup.ce.missing.hint: Subscribe to it on the Steam Workshop (package id {id}) and scan again. Vanilla design works without it.
setup.ce.unknown: Scan the library to find out whether Combat Extended is in it.
setup.settings.title: Settings
setup.settings.hint: A read only summary. The settings file is plain text; edit it by hand if you need to change something.
setup.settings.error: The settings could not be read
designer.clone.unchanged: Nothing differs from the source yet.

designer.definition.title: Definition of {name}
designer.drafts.deleteBody: The draft {name} is removed from the project. Files already written stay.
designer.drafts.emptyBody: Start a new weapon, or clone one from the reference list.
designer.editor.emptyBody: Pick a draft on the left, start a new weapon, or clone one from the reference list.
designer.estimate.anchored: This draft is anchored to {source}. The fit meter compares it with that weapon and its peers.
designer.estimate.fill: Fill empty fields from the estimate
designer.estimate.filledNone: No empty field had a suggestion.
designer.estimate.title: Estimate
designer.field.label: Label
designer.fit.defaultBands: These bands are the defaults, not measured from the weapons of your install. Calibrate to measure them.
designer.fit.none: Nothing to score yet. Type or fill the numbers first.
designer.fit.optimistic: Bands may be optimistic: many near twins in the pool.
designer.fit.rough: Bands are rough: few reference weapons behind them.
designer.fit.typicalityHelp: Typicality runs from 0 to 100. Low means unusual, not wrong.
designer.fit.waiting: The fit appears after the first preview.
designer.help.capacities: Comma separated, for example Cut, Stab
designer.help.defName: Letters, digits and underscores. A loaded def with the same name is refused.
designer.help.parent: The base def this weapon inherits from. Inherited stats are not repeated.
designer.other.inheritedHelp: These stats come from the parent base and are not written to the definition.
designer.output.apply.backup: Back up files that are replaced
designer.output.apply.backupHelp: A file that already exists is copied to the RimStudio backups folder of this project before it is replaced. Backups are never placed inside the mod folder, so they are not uploaded with it.
designer.output.apply.dry: Check the Combat Extended patch against the definitions after writing
designer.output.apply.intro: These files will be written under {folder}:
designer.output.apply.title: Apply to project
designer.output.apply.unchanged.one: {n} file is already up to date and is left alone.
designer.output.apply.unchanged.other: {n} files are already up to date and are left alone.
designer.output.blocked.errors: Fix the errors in the problems list before writing.
designer.output.blocked.errorsCount.one: Fix the {n} error in the problems list before writing.
designer.output.blocked.errorsCount.othe: Fix the {n} errors in the problems list before writing.
designer.output.blocked.failed: The plan could not be made. See the message above.
designer.output.blocked.noDraft: Open a draft to apply it.
designer.output.blocked.nothing: Everything is already written and up to date.
designer.output.blocked.planning: Waiting for the plan to update.
designer.output.ce.allAnswered: Every Combat Extended question is answered.
designer.output.ce.explain: Off by default. The weapon is always written as a plain RimWorld definition. When this is on, a separate patch file is added in {folder} and LoadFolders.xml loads that folder only when Combat Extended is active.
designer.output.ce.explainNoFolder: Off by default. The weapon is always written as a plain RimWorld definition. When this is on, a separate patch file is added in the Combat Extended folder of the mod and LoadFolders.xml loads that folder only when Combat Extended is active.
designer.output.ce.noData: Combat Extended data is not loaded.
designer.output.ce.offHelp: Turn this on to see the numbers Combat Extended needs and the questions you have to answer.
designer.output.ce.takeHelp: A derived value is only written when you take it. Each one is listed under Derived values once the plan is made.
designer.output.ce.title: Combat Extended
designer.output.noDraft: Open a draft to see its output.
designer.output.patchWaits: The Combat Extended patch files appear once every answer is given.
designer.output.result.allWritten: Every file of the plan was written.
designer.output.result.dryFailed: The patch did not load cleanly
designer.output.result.dryFailedBody: The Combat Extended patch was tried against the definitions and reported problems. See the notes below.
designer.output.result.dryOk: The Combat Extended patch loads against the definitions.
designer.output.result.noBackup: No file was replaced, so no backup was needed.
designer.output.result.unchanged.one: {n} file was already up to date.
designer.output.result.unchanged.other: {n} files were already up to date.
designer.output.source.identity: same as vanilla, from {n} converted weapons
designer.panel.other: Other fields copied from the source
designer.project.none: No project is open. Drafts are stored in a project folder.
designer.projectile.sharedNote: The damage and armor penetration written to the definition come from this projectile def. Switch to an own projectile to write the damage typed here.
designer.quiz.closer: Which weapon is the new one closer to?
designer.quiz.compare: Compared with the {label}, the new weapon should be
designer.quiz.finished: The estimate is ready. Use the button below the quiz to fill the empty fields.
designer.quiz.group: Which group does the weapon belong to?
designer.quiz.role: What role does the weapon have?
designer.quiz.title: Estimate quiz
designer.quiz.vsAnchor: Compared with the {label}, is {stat} lower, similar or higher?
designer.readout.waiting: The readouts appear after the first preview.
designer.reference.emptyBody: No weapon matches the filters, or no game install is set up.
designer.structure.title: Suggested structure
designer.tools.none: No tools yet. A melee weapon needs at least one.
designer.raw.badShape: A node needs a tag, a list of attributes (name and value pairs) and a list of children (text or nodes).
designer.raw.treeHelp: A field with attributes or child elements is edited as a tree: a tag, a list of attributes as name and value pairs, and a list of children. The app checks the result and reports problems under the field.
designer.raw.valueHelp: The text between the tags. Leave it empty for an empty element.
designer.tool.otherFieldsHelp: Fields of this tool that have no input of their own. They are written as they are.
designer.tool.surpriseDamages: Extra damages of the surprise attack
designer.recipe.none: No recipe settings. The recipe is built from the cost list unless you add settings here.
designer.recipe.otherFieldsHelp: Recipe fields that have no input of their own, such as the work speed stat. They are written as they are.
designer.recipe.skillsHelp: The skill level a colonist needs to make the weapon. A row without a skill or a level is not written.
designer.recipe.title: Recipe
designer.other.compsHelp: The comps of the definition, one li entry each.
designer.other.fieldsHelp: Fields of the definition that have no input of their own. They are written as they are and checked when you export.
designer.other.offsetsHelp: Stats the wearer gains or loses while holding the weapon.
designer.other.verbExtra: Other fields of the shooting verb
designer.other.verbExtraHelp: Fields of the shooting verb that have no input of their own.
designer.other.verbsHelp: Verbs besides the shooting verb, one li entry each.
designer.help.tradeTags: What traders and quest rewards use to find the weapon.
designer.help.weaponClasses: Groups the weapon for the game, for example Ranged or LongShots.
designer.help.weaponTags: What raiders and pawn generators use to pick the weapon, for example Gun.
designer.look.help: Point at art that exists in the game or in your mod. To bring your own PNG, use the Texture panel.
designer.look.graphicExtraHelp: Fields of the graphic data that have no input of their own.
designer.identity.tierInherited: The parent base supplies the tier: {tier}.
designer.projectile.fieldsHelp: Fields of the projectile that have no input of their own, such as explosion fields.
designer.projectile.ownHelp: This weapon has its own projectile definition. Its damage, speed and armor penetration are written to your mod, so editing the damage changes the written file.
designer.projectile.sharedHelp: This weapon points at a projectile that already exists. The damage written to the definition comes from that projectile, so editing the damage here only changes the numbers shown on this page, not the written file. Turn on Own projectile to write your own damage.
designer.carried.missing: The source weapon does not set these required fields either, so they are not errors: {fields}.
designer.carried.omittedHelp: These fields are not written because the parent supplies them.
designer.carried.resetHelp: These lists are written with Inherit="False", so they do not add to the lists of the parent.
designer.cloneNotes.label: Notes about the clone
designer.dialog.ownProjectile: Give the clone its own projectile
designer.dialog.ownProjectileHelp: The projectile of the source is copied under a new name, so changing the damage changes the written file. Turn it off to keep pointing at the source projectile.
designer.other.more: Components, other verbs and verb fields

project.guide.label: Folder roles
project.guide.intro: The RimStudio layout keeps the names RimWorld itself uses. The roles below are the badges of the folder tree.
project.guide.about: Name, package id, supported versions. Required.
project.guide.load-folders: Which folders load for which game version or mod. Only when needed.
project.guide.content-root: A version folder or Common, when the mod keeps its content there.
project.guide.defs-weapons: One file per weapon, holding its projectile first, in a folder named after the category.
project.guide.patches: Patches for the base game and other mods, never for Combat Extended.
project.guide.ce-compat: Combat Extended patches. Loaded only when that mod is active.
project.guide.textures: Images named by the texPath of a definition. The tool never makes images.
project.guide.sounds: Sound clips named by the clipFolderPath of a sound definition.
project.guide.source: Author material the game never reads, such as layered art.
project.guide.rule.perWeapon: A new weapon is a new file. A second weapon never edits the first.
project.guide.rule.vanilla: Definitions are always vanilla. Combat Extended content is a separate patch, added only when you ask for it.
project.guide.rule.keep: A mod that follows another convention keeps it. Nothing is moved without your say.
project.new.title: New mod
project.new.parent.hint: The folder that will hold the new mod folder.
project.new.name: Mod name
project.new.author: Author
project.new.packageId.hint: Suggested from the author and the name. Letters, digits and dots.
project.new.versions.hint: Separate several with commas, for example 1.5, 1.6.
project.new.description.hint: Optional. A placeholder is written when it is empty.
project.new.error: The mod could not be created
project.new.opt.placeholders: Keep empty folders with a placeholder file
project.new.opt.ignoreSource: Keep Source art out of the repository

patches.title: Patches
patches.view.label: Patches view
patches.include-converted: Show weapons that are already converted
patches.select-all.one: Select the {n} weapon that can be converted
patches.select-all.other: Select all {n} weapons that can be converted
patches.split.label: Resize the weapon list
patches.noproject.title: No mod is open
patches.noproject.body: Choose the folder of the mod whose weapons you want to convert. The folder is read and only the Combat Extended patch files are written.
patches.missing.title: The mod folder was not found
patches.missing.body: The folder {path} could not be opened. It may have been moved or deleted.
patches.ce.title: Combat Extended is not available
patches.ce.body: Weapons can only be converted when the Combat Extended files of your install are known, because the numbers are read from them.
patches.ce.link: Check the Combat Extended folder on the Setup page
patches.scan.running: Scanning the weapons of the mod. The first scan reads the game and Combat Extended and can take a few seconds.
patches.scan.diagnostics: Problems found while reading the mod
patches.empty.title: No weapons found
patches.empty.body: This mod has no weapon definitions that can be converted. Weapons are read from the definition files of the mod.
patches.counts.label: Scan result
patches.table.label: Weapons of the mod
patches.chips.label: Tags and classes
patches.detail.not-convertible: This weapon cannot be converted. The reason is given above.
patches.questions.none: Nothing is left to ask. The numbers are derived from the weapon and from your converted weapons.
patches.scope.label: Apply answers to
patches.scope.family-help: Answers given here apply to every weapon of the family {family}. An answer given for a single weapon wins over the family answer.
patches.rank.used-damage: used by {n} converted weapons, first damage {damage}
patches.rank.note: The {n} choices at the top are ranked by how closely converted weapons with similar tags use them.
patches.plan.open-body: No file is planned until every question is answered. The numbers below are what the generator derived so far.
patches.plan.nothing-converted: This weapon already carries a conversion and the plan changes nothing.
patches.plan.ready.one: The plan is ready: {n} file will be written.
patches.plan.ready.other: The plan is ready: {n} files will be written.
patches.plan.derived-help: These numbers were not answered by you. Each one is copied from the weapon or predicted from your converted weapons; check the rated ones.
patches.derived.label: Derived numbers
patches.definition.none: The file of this weapon is not known.
patches.definition.truncated: The file is longer than what is shown.
patches.definition.label: Text of {path}
patches.apply.title: Apply the conversion
patches.apply.loadfolders-create: A new LoadFolders.xml is created. It loads the Combat Extended patch folder only when Combat Extended is active.
patches.apply.loadfolders-edit: LoadFolders.xml is edited. The Combat Extended patch folder is added so that it loads only when Combat Extended is active; the rest of the file is kept.
patches.apply.backup: Back up files that are replaced
patches.apply.backup-where: Backups go to the project backups folder inside the app data folder, never into the mod folder. The report lists each backup path.
patches.apply.backup-none: Every file is new, so there is nothing to back up.
patches.apply.dry: Test the patch on a scratch copy after writing
patches.report.ok: Every file was written and read back.
patches.report.partial: Some weapons were not applied. What was written stays in the mod.
patches.report.skipped: The plan had errors, so nothing was written for this weapon.
patches.lint.none.title: Nothing to check
patches.lint.none.body: The mod has no patch file to check.
patches.lint.help: The rules (CEP) run over every patch file of the mod, written by hand or generated, against the {version} load folder. A file is read and never changed.
patches.lint.no-ce-data: Combat Extended is not loaded, so the rules that compare against its data did not run.
patches.lint.scan: Problems found while reading the mod
patches.lint.not-checked-help: These rules need data that is not available yet, so the result above does not cover them.
patches.lint.not-checked.label: Rules that did not run
patches.apply.shared: shared by {n} weapons, written one after the other
designer.reference.loading: Reading the weapons of your install
designer.assets.kind.unknown: Not a PNG, WAV or Ogg file
designer.assets.neverCopied: Textures of the game are never copied. A shared texture stays a path to the game's own file. Only a PNG you import here is copied into your mod, and only when you apply.
designer.assets.origin.imported: Imported file. It is copied to {target} in your mod and the definition points there.
designer.assets.origin.importedPending: Imported file. It is copied into the texture folder of your mod when you apply.
designer.assets.origin.reserved: No texture yet. The definition gets the reserved texture path of your mod, ready for a PNG you add later.
designer.assets.origin.shared: Shared texture {texPath}. The path is written as it is; the game's own file is not copied.
designer.assets.projectileNeedsOwn: A projectile texture needs an own projectile. Turn on Own projectile in the Projectile panel.
designer.assets.status.refused: The file cannot be used: it is a link, a folder or not a regular file.
designer.assets.status.tooLarge: The file is larger than the limit.
designer.output.apply.copies.one: 1 of these files is copied from your computer.
designer.output.apply.copies.other: {n} of these files are copied from your computer.
designer.output.copy.replaces: A different file is at the target now (SHA-256 {hash}). It is backed up before it is replaced.
designer.sounds.bothEnds: Enter both numbers to write the range.
designer.sounds.clipsHelp: WAV or Ogg files. They are copied into the Sounds folder of your mod, and a sound definition is written for them.
designer.sounds.defNameHelp: Leave empty to name it after the weapon.
designer.sounds.distanceHelp: In tiles. Leave empty for the game default.
designer.sounds.equipHelp: Played when a pawn handles the weapon, for example picks it up.
designer.sounds.help: A sound is a sound definition, chosen by name from the game or made from clips you bring. Clips are copied into your mod when you apply.
designer.sounds.noClips: No clips yet. Add a WAV or Ogg file.
designer.sounds.pitchHelp: 1 is the pitch of the clip itself. Leave empty for the game default.
designer.sounds.plan.none: Nothing is written for the shot sound yet. Add a clip and fix the problems above.
designer.sounds.plan.title: What will be written
designer.sounds.shotSource: Where the shot sound comes from
designer.sounds.showing: First {shown} of {total} sounds. Type to narrow the list.
designer.sounds.volumeHelp: In the game's scale. Leave empty for the game default.
designer.look.textureImported: A PNG is imported for the weapon, so the written file points at its copy instead of this path.
ceblock.bow.title: Bow, ammo and reload
ceblock.bow.help: These members are written only when you set them. A bow is recognised from its shape unless you say otherwise.
ceblock.bow.kindHelp: A bow gets an arrow ammo set, no magazine and no reload.
ceblock.bow.perMagHelp: How much ammo a pawn's kit gets for each magazine of this weapon.
ceblock.bow.massHelp: Leave empty to keep the vanilla mass.
ceblock.bow.runAndGunHelp: Whether a pawn may fire the weapon while moving.
ceblock.bow.reload: Reload one round at a time
ceblock.bow.reloadHelp: For shotguns and other weapons that load one round per reload step.
ceblock.bow.recoilHelp: The name of a recoil pattern of Combat Extended. Leave empty for none.
ceblock.tags.title: Companion weapon tags
ceblock.tags.label: Weapon tags to add
ceblock.tags.help: Extra tags written next to the weapon tag class. They are never added unless you list them.
ceblock.tools.title: Tool list
ceblock.tools.help: Without a list the tools of the vanilla weapon are carried over. With a list the tools are written as given, so a muzzle tool or a split of capacities is your choice.
ceblock.tools.label: Label
ceblock.tools.labelHelp: The label of the tool in the converted weapon. It may be empty.
ceblock.tools.fromHelp: The vanilla tool this one is made from. Empty means the tool with the same label.
ceblock.tools.capacitiesHelp: Leave empty to keep the capacities of the vanilla tool.
ceblock.tools.keepHelp: Fields of the vanilla tools that the conversion keeps instead of replacing.
ceblock.platform.title: Weapon platform
ceblock.platform.help: A platform accepts attachments. Fill this in only for a weapon that does.
ceblock.link.attachmentHelp: The definition name of the attachment.
ceblock.link.vectorHelp: Written as the game writes a vector.
ceblock.stat.name: {label} stat
ceblock.part.slotsHelp: The slots this part belongs to.
ceblock.ub.title: Under barrel unit
ceblock.ub.help: A second firing mode under the barrel, such as a grenade launcher. Its numbers are asked, not guessed.
ceblock.ub.flag: This weapon has an under barrel unit
ceblock.ub.oneHolder: Shares the ammo of the weapon
ceblock.ub.ammoSetHelp: A unit that shares the ammo of the weapon needs none.
ceblock.ub.projectileHelp: Empty means the first projectile of the ammo set.
ceblock.ub.replacesHelp: The vanilla component the unit takes over from.
ceblock.raw.title: Other elements
ceblock.raw.label: Elements written into the patch
ceblock.raw.help: An element is written as given. The webview does not read XML: describe it as a tree (a tag, attributes and children as JSON) or add a simple one by name. The backend checks every element when the plan is built.
ceblock.raw.badJson: The text is not valid JSON.
ceblock.options.title: Suggested by your conversions
ceblock.options.help: Combat Extended conversions you already have share these habits. Nothing is written until you take one.
designer.output.ce.extrasHelp: Optional parts for bows, platforms and special cases. Each group says what it holds; nothing is written until you set it.
patches.options.help: Optional parts of the conversion: bows, ammo extras, companion tags, an explicit tool list, platforms, the under barrel unit and other elements. Nothing is written unless you set it.
patches.options.familyHelp: What you set here applies to every weapon of the family {family} that does not set its own.
patches.questions.skip-under-barrel: Leave the under barrel unit out of the conversion
